title: Prepare
what: Read what the machine is and what it allows before anything is changed: the stock system, the boot facts, the way back.

title: Boot
what: Get an image of ours accepted by the bootloader and run, one part swapped at a time, until it is known what refuses it.

title: Console
what: A window onto the running kernel: a banner, a shell, over UART or the USB gadget.

title: Kernel
what: Our kernel builds, reaches its init and says nothing worse than it should.

title: Power
what: The PMIC, the charger and the watchdog: what keeps the machine alive and safe to leave running.

title: Storage
what: Internal storage seen, first read-only.

title: Userspace
what: A distribution's root boots, the network is up and the health suite runs on every boot.

title: Coprocessors
what: The processors a phone leans on - the modem's, the audio and sensor DSPs, the Wi-Fi core - get their firmware, run, and stay up.

title: Display and input
what: The panel lights, touch and keys answer, the GPU renders.

title: Sound
what: The card, the codec and the amplifiers, a profile for the shell, sound heard and recorded.

title: Modem, SMS and data
what: The modem seen, the SIM read, the network joined; messages and data both ways.

title: Calls
what: A call with sound both ways, the screen dark at the ear, emergency numbers known, calls over LTE.

title: Local radios
what: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, NFC, USB host and sharing the connection.

title: Sensors and location
what: Motion, light and proximity read and used; a position fix; the fingerprint reader.

title: Camera
what: From the camera bus to a photo and a video: sensor, raw frame, a viewable stream, focus and flash.

title: Sleep and battery life
what: Suspend that returns, wakes only for what matters and reaches the SoC's floor; a day on one charge.

title: Goals
what: The steps that only name a whole: Linux runs, a daily-usable phone, a complete phone - each done when all it needs is.

title: Lab
what: What the lab needs of a machine to work on it without hands: the ways in, a try that cannot brick, and a hardware-test layer with no shell to suspend, lock or answer keys on its own.

title: Updates and endurance
what: Updates that apply and roll back, and the phone still working after days, upgrades and crashes of its parts.

title: Shell
what: The phone shell - sxmo, Phosh or Plasma Mobile - as a layer after the proven hardware: it runs on it, locks, types, notifies, rotates and holds its own idle suspend.
